text:
Matthew Schaefer keeps finding his name next to legends. The Islanders' young defenseman tied a Bobby Orr mark this month, scored a power-play goal in his 100th game, and has 13 points in his last ten. He's the reason to watch this team, and the reason the rebuild around him feels faster than anyone planned.

The record is better than the play. New York is 9-6-4 with 22 points, but it has taken under 46% of all expected goals (the quality of chances) and 48% at five on five. Our points model has them about five points above what their play has earned, and the goaltending explains it: the team has allowed 12.7 fewer goals than its chances. Semyon Varlamov, back from injury, has saved 4.7 goals above expected over his last five starts.

The California trip went 2-0-1 and ended with a 6-2 win in Anaheim: a Simon Holmstrom hat trick, three points for Schaefer, and a strong return for Mathew Barzal. Ryan Pulock and Matias Maccelli are back too. The cost was Logan Stanley, Schaefer's partner, who left with a lower-body injury, and Bo Horvat sat the final four minutes.

Victor Eklund is the other rookie worth your time, learning beside Brayden Schenn on a line that has outscored teams 8-1. Our playoff odds sit at 29%. What we'd watch: who plays with Schaefer now, and how long the saves cover for the chances.
